The Camera in the Tree: 学生在校园树上安装相机观察鸟类。
Science lovers at Green Hill School had a question: which birds visit the old oak tree in the yard every year? Nobody knew the answer, because the birds only came when people were not around.

Their science teacher, Mr Park, had an idea. With the school's help, the students put a small camera on a branch of the oak tree. The camera had a movement sensor: every time a bird landed, it started to record automatically.

For three months, the students checked the videos twice a week. They were amazed by the results. Eleven different kinds of birds visited the tree, including two kinds that nobody had seen in the town for years. A fox also appeared one night, and once a cat from the neighbourhood sat on the branch for a whole afternoon.

The students wrote a report with their photos and sent it to a nature magazine. To their surprise, the magazine printed it and called the project 'a model for young scientists'. The camera is still in the tree. Who knows what will visit the old oak next spring?
